title: The Scunthorpe Test: a profanity-filter benchmark where blocking Scunthorpe counts against you
description:
A benchmark for profanity filters that reports how many innocent words a filter blocks beside how much profanity it catches: plain profanity, every disguise technique alone and combined (leetspeak, homoglyphs, spacing, zero-width characters), usernames, contextual cases, a Civil Comments sample of running text, and innocent words and phrases that contain a profane string, such as Scunthorpe. Each label is a function of the data.

This archive carries the public dev split, the runner, adapters for open-source filters and the published results. The data is under CC BY 4.0 and the code under MIT. The leaderboard and the method: unprofane.com/bench/scunthorpe.
